owner.name: Sai Vardhan Makkapati
about: I'm an agentic AI developer. I build systems that reason about a goal, pick the right tools, act, and check their own work — not demos that stop at a model call.
What keeps me here is the engineering around the model: the loop, the memory, the evaluation. That's where an idea turns into something that actually runs.

experience.note: Built and deployed an AWS-hosted autonomous LLM interview platform — resume/JD matching, a two-stage LLM screening pipeline, and rubric-driven candidate evaluation.
Building and shipping AI systems as an AI engineer.

stack.intro: Everything below is something I've actually built with — an agent framework, a production interview platform, or a project on BUILDS. Not a checklist of frameworks I've only read about.

projects.title: AGENTLAB
projects.blurb: A local platform for running tool-using agents safely, attacking them with prompt injection, and debugging their runs step by step.
highlights: MCP Gateway: one endpoint for any client, with default-deny policies, human approvals, snapshots + rollback and an audit log
Arena: 12 prompt-injection attacks across 3 fake scenarios, scored against pluggable defenses in a matrix runner
Recorder: every run as a timeline — replay with recorded tool results, fork, diff two runs, golden regression suites
CLI bridge turns installed tools (git, gh, docker) into MCP tools from YAML manifests, with argument-injection guards
Admin UI with live approvals, audit, policy simulator and run waterfall; 128 tests

projects.title: AI CODING ASSISTANT
projects.blurb: An agent framework with real tool-calling: it reads and edits code, runs commands, searches the web and keeps its own memory.
highlights: Model Context Protocol servers over both stdio and HTTP/SSE transports
12+ built-in tools — file edit, glob, grep, shell, web fetch, memory, todo
Context compression and token budgeting to survive long sessions
Approval policies with dangerous-command detection before anything mutates
Session persistence — save, resume and checkpoint conversations

projects.title: STORY CREW
projects.blurb: A multi-agent crew that writes illustrated children's stories — one crew drafts, another critiques and suggests.
highlights: Separate story-writing and suggestion crews with their own roles and tasks
Swappable LLM backends — Groq inference and hosted HuggingFace endpoints
Task graph defined independently of the agents that execute it

projects.title: LANGGRAPH CHAT
projects.blurb: A streaming chat assistant built as an explicit LangGraph state machine, running entirely against a local model.
highlights: Conversation modelled as a typed graph state rather than a prompt string
Checkpointed memory so threads survive across turns
Runs offline on local Llama 3.2 — no API key, no data leaving the machine

projects.title: CHURN PIPELINE
projects.blurb: Customer churn prediction wired as a reproducible pipeline — versioned data, tracked experiments, containerised runs.
highlights: DVC stages make the ETL and training run reproducible from a lockfile
MLflow tracking for runs, params and model artifacts
Config-driven so a rerun is a file change, not a code change

projects.title: NETWORK SECURITY ML
projects.blurb: An end-to-end pipeline for network threat classification, from MongoDB ingestion through to a packaged model.
highlights: Schema-validated ingestion — bad data fails at the boundary, not in training
Artifact directory per run, so every stage's output is inspectable
Packaged with setup.py and a Dockerfile for deployment

projects.title: HOUSING PRICE PIPELINE
projects.blurb: Price regression built as composable pipeline steps with a separate deployment path, not a single notebook.
highlights: Training and deployment split into separate runnable entry points
Steps written as reusable units rather than inline cells
MLflow run history kept alongside the analysis notebooks

projects.title: STOCK FORECAST PIPELINE
projects.blurb: A configuration-driven forecasting service — parameters live in YAML, the code stays the same.
highlights: params.yaml drives the run; no hard-coded hyperparameters
Structured src/config/logs layout with a research folder kept separate
Containerised for a consistent runtime

projects.title: TEXT SUMMARIZER
projects.blurb: An end-to-end NLP summarisation service, taking a transformer model from data prep through to a served endpoint.
highlights: Ingestion, validation, transformation, training and evaluation split into discrete pipeline stages
schema.yaml and params.yaml drive validation and hyperparameters — no hard-coded config in the pipeline code
Flask endpoint serves the trained model directly off the same pipeline artifacts
Packaged with a Dockerfile and setup.py for a repeatable deploy

projects.title: WINE QUALITY
projects.blurb: A wine-quality regression model served behind a small Flask app, with an HTML form for live predictions rather than just a notebook.
highlights: Same config-driven pipeline shape as the other MLOps projects — schema.yaml, params.yaml, staged src/ pipeline
Flask + Jinja templates give it an actual form to submit inputs against, not just a CLI
Packaged with a Dockerfile so the trained model and the app ship together

projects.title: FOOTBALL MATCH ANALYSIS
projects.blurb: Automated analysis of match footage — who is on the pitch, which team has the ball, and how far everyone ran.
highlights: Detects and separates players, referees, goalkeepers and the ball
Assigns teams dynamically from kit colour rather than fixed labels
Estimates ball possession, player speed and distance covered
Compensates for camera movement so motion is measured in pitch space

projects.title: MEDICAL IMAGING SUITE
projects.blurb: A set of cancer classifiers across four imaging modalities, each trained and evaluated on its own dataset.
highlights: Breast histopathology and ultrasound, kidney, and lung CT classifiers
Transfer learning with VGG19 alongside models trained from scratch
Each modality kept as its own reproducible notebook

projects.title: FASHION GAN
projects.blurb: A generative adversarial network that synthesises black-and-white fashion imagery from noise.
highlights: Trained on FashionMNIST — 60k training / 10k test grayscale images across 10 clothing classes
Generator upsamples a 128-dim noise vector through transposed convolutions from 7×7 to a 28×28 image
Discriminator is a convolutional binary classifier trained adversarially against it
Custom TensorFlow training loop rather than a stock Keras .fit() call

projects.title: IMAGE CAPTIONING
projects.blurb: An encoder-decoder captioning model trained on COCO — vision features in, natural language out.
highlights: InceptionV3 (ImageNet-pretrained, top layers stripped) as the CNN feature encoder
Transformer encoder-decoder generates the caption from those features rather than an RNN
10,000 image-caption pairs sampled from COCO, tokenized to a 15k-word vocabulary with [start]/[end] markers
80/20 train-validation split with a tf.data pipeline (shuffle, batch, prefetch) feeding training

projects.title: GESTURE RECOGNITION
projects.blurb: A CNN that classifies hand gestures for television control from short video clips.
highlights: Frame-sequence classification rather than single-image prediction
Trained on a five-gesture TV-remote control vocabulary
Kept as a single self-contained notebook — data loading through evaluation in one place

projects.title: HAND CONTROL
projects.blurb: Real-time hand tracking that drives system volume and the mouse cursor straight from a webcam.
highlights: MediaPipe Hands for landmark tracking, no training step of its own
Volume scales continuously with the thumb-to-index-finger distance
Index finger alone moves the cursor; raising index + middle together fires a right-click

projects.title: EMOTION DETECTION
projects.blurb: Facial emotion classification, kept as a clean data / models / notebooks split.
highlights: Dataset, trained models and experiments separated into their own directories rather than interleaved
CNN classifier trained directly on labelled facial-expression images

projects.title: RECOMENDA
projects.blurb: A book recommender built on collaborative filtering, shipped as a deployable app rather than a notebook.
highlights: K-nearest-neighbour collaborative filtering over a user-book matrix
Modular ML pipeline structure with the app layered on top
Containerised for deployment

projects.title: NEWS SENTIMENT SIGNALS
projects.blurb: Turns financial news sentiment into a tradeable signal, with training and evaluation kept separate.
highlights: Dedicated data_processing module turns raw news text into model-ready features
Separate trainer and tester scripts, with test results written out rather than just printed
Sentiment scores joined against price data to produce the actual trading signal
